newsitem.title: USA: Cash grade trade leaves differentials even in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Cash grade trade leaves differentials even in U.S.

text.p: Cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf held onto moderate gains in the outright market Friday afternoon on technical buying and continued jitters over the timing for renewed Iraqi crude exports, traders said.
For the cash grades, differentials failed to adjust from the morning, leaving most barrels priced at the same levels established on Thursday.

July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was pegged around $19.00-10 a barrel, 15 cents firmer than Thursday. At 1416 EDT/1816 GMT, July NYMEX futures were 15 cents higher at $18.84 a barrel, compared with August futures at a more robust $19.12 a barrel, leaving the roll around -27 cents.
Deals were confirmed for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at 14 and 15 cents under July WTI/Cushing cash, steady from the late session Thursday chatter.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire pushed slightly stronger with deals at 50 and 45 cents under the cash marker.
WTI/Midland barrels found favor at 37 cents under, steady from late Thursday.
West Texas Sour/Midland was talked at $1.45-58 under WTI/Cushing, with Eugene Island around a $2.04 discount.
WTI/Cushing sold out to $1.92, but has fallen back to $1.85, traders said.
